mission: Protect membrane fats from oxidative damage so vulnerable polyunsaturated fatty acids remain intact.

stage2a.operation: Owns lipid-peroxyl chain termination; regeneration belongs to PM6 and transcriptional regulation to Nrf2/NF-kB. Existing null/high-dose limits retained.

existing_findings.proposition: Vitamin E interrupts lipid peroxidation by scavenging peroxyl radicals in the lipid phase. Its vitamin function is protection of polyunsaturated fats in membranes.

existing_source_assessments.label: Niki (2014)
existing_source_assessments.exposure_context: in vitro lipid peroxidation and in vivo kinetic evidence
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Vitamin E breaks peroxyl-radical chain propagation in vitro and in vivo, and is not an efficient scavenger of several other radicals in vivo.

assessment.study: Review of kinetic and physiological evidence for vitamin E as a peroxyl-radical scavenger.
assessment.population: Chemical systems and the in vivo molar ratio of vitamin E to its substrates. No new human cohort.
assessment.result: Vitamin E inhibits lipid peroxidation by breaking peroxyl-radical chains. Other radicals are not scavenged efficiently at physiological ratios.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No dietary dose-response. The claim is which radical vitamin E can stop.
assessment.evidence_summary: Vitamin E is the chain-breaking antioxidant in the lipid phase.
assessment.limitations: A review of chemistry is not an intake trial and not a brain-outcome trial.

existing_source_assessments.label: Traber and Atkinson (2007)
existing_source_assessments.exposure_context: review of the in vivo vitamin function
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: The vitamin function of alpha-tocopherol is peroxyl-radical scavenging that protects polyunsaturated fats in membranes.

assessment.study: Review arguing that the in vivo actions of alpha-tocopherol follow from peroxyl-radical scavenging.
assessment.population: Mammalian vitamin E biology. No new trial.
assessment.result: Protecting polyunsaturated fats in membranes is the vitamin function.
assessment.effect_magnitude: No intake threshold for peroxidation is set.
assessment.evidence_summary: The membrane job of vitamin E is protection of polyunsaturated fats.
assessment.limitations: The review does not measure peroxidation after a change in intake.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

existing_findings.proposition: A long prevention trial found more prostate cancers with 400 IU of vitamin E a day than with placebo. That result is not a peroxidation measurement, and it is a reason not to treat extra vitamin E as a benefit.

existing_source_assessments.label: Klein et al. (2011)
existing_source_assessments.exposure_context: 400 IU vitamin E a day in a prevention trial
existing_source_assessments.directional_finding: Vitamin E assignment was associated with more prostate cancers than placebo.

assessment.study: SELECT prevention trial of selenium and vitamin E, with extended follow-up for prostate cancer.
assessment.population: Men without prostate cancer at entry, assigned vitamin E, selenium, both, or placebo.
assessment.result: Vitamin E, 400 IU a day, was associated with a higher prostate-cancer risk than placebo.
assessment.effect_magnitude: The paper reports a higher risk. It does not report a peroxidation marker.
assessment.evidence_summary: Extra vitamin E at this dose is not a benefit.
assessment.limitations: Cancer incidence is not membrane peroxidation, so the trial does not test the chain-breaking reaction.

existing_findings.disposition: Existing canonical assessment retained; enrichment is additive. No clinical or source-level negative inferred from bounded retrieval.

stage2a.evidence_enrichment: Chemical chain-breaking and deficient-cell oxidative challenge support a bounded vitamin E role. The existing high-dose prevention-trial harm remains an important clinical limit, not a peroxidation-rate measurement.

source_to_claim_records.proposition: Alpha-tocopherol supports lipid-phase peroxyl-radical chain termination.
source_to_claim_records.limitation: Vitamin E forms differ in retention; high-dose benefits and brain efficacy are not inferred.

source_to_claim_records.proposition: Deficiency/repletion and ex-vivo erythrocyte observations corroborate lipid-protection capacity.
source_to_claim_records.limitation: Erythrocyte oxidative challenge is not brain efficacy or a general high-dose prescription.

stage2a.coverage_limitations: Existing source assessments and full attached bibliography are inventoried and preserved. Targeted source retrieval is bounded to the stated propositions; unrefreshed clinical/Phenome sources are not newly validated. No evidence of absence is inferred.
stage2a.stop_rationale: Preserve the complete baseline, add the bounded supported evidence and exact qualifications, and park material attribution/traceability questions for approval instead of forcing an admission or expanding to a comprehensive rebuild.
